category_title: Highly resistant students with autism and severe communication impairment
minimal_context: Hannah and a tutor are in an individual work session looking at a book with lift and reveal flaps.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's sit down and look at this lift and reveal flap book together.

STUDENT: (Takes the book and begins looking rapidly through it independently, appearing to be absorbed in it.)

TUTOR: Let me help you turn the page and see what is under this flap.

STUDENT: (Turns away from the adult and pushes the adult's hand away from the book.)

TUTOR: We need to read this together. Look at this page.

STUDENT: (Moves away, pushes the adult away, and goes back to spending time looking at the book independently to withdraw from the attempt to interact.)

options.A: Adjust the ratio of lower-level to higher-level questions based on the student's reading level during the session.
options.B: Follow the student's lead rather than following a curriculum and setting out to teach her something.
options.C: Ask lower-level questions focused primarily on having the student recall factual information about the book's characters or plot.
options.D: Highlight high-quality reading miscues with praise, focus on miscues affecting meaning, and do not count dialects as errors.
